activities.caption: call the magnitude — the stakes on the curve
activities.name: acwCensusEstimate

config.prompt: The 1860 census enumerated roughly how many people as enslaved?
config.why: 3.95 million — property worth something like $3 billion, more than all the country's factories and railways combined, demanding constant new land because cotton exhausts soil within a decade.
config.context: From just under 700,000 in 1790, the curve grew about 30 per cent per decade, almost entirely through natural increase.

activities.anchor: The quarrel was manageable only while there was new territory
activities.caption: line up the bargains and the collapse, earliest first
activities.name: acwCompromiseOrder

config.prompt: Compromise and collapse — order them, earliest first:
items: the Missouri Compromise draws the line at 36°30′ — 1820
the Compromise of 1850 admits California free but gives the South a ferocious Fugitive Slave Act
the Kansas-Nebraska Act lets settlers vote slavery up or down — 'Bleeding Kansas' — 1854
the Dred Scott decision voids every compromise retroactively — 1857
John Brown tries to start the uprising himself — 1859
config.why: Each crisis made the other section look less like a partner and more like an enemy — and when the land ran out in the 1850s, the differences had to be settled.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the human bill
activities.name: acwRightsSpot

config.prompt: One line of this war-cost briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Roughly 620,000 soldiers died by the traditional count.
A 2011 demographic study by J. David Hacker put the true total near 750,000.
That is about 2.5 per cent of the entire US population — proportionately equivalent to over 8 million Americans today.
The South recovered its pre-war income per head within a decade.
Railways moved armies, the telegraph moved news, and both sides fought total war against economies as well as armies.
config.correction: The South lost a generation of its white male workforce and did not recover its pre-war income per head until the twentieth century.
config.why: The war was also the first 'modern' war — rifled muskets and ironclads made old tactics lethal, culminating in Sherman's deliberate targeting of Southern infrastructure.

activities.caption: pair each step of 1860–61 with its date
activities.name: acwElectionMatch

config.prompt: The sectional victory — pair each fact with its date:

pairs.left: under 40 per cent of the popular vote
pairs.right: Lincoln's 1860 share — on the ballot in none of ten southern states
South Carolina secedes, before Lincoln even takes office
six states form the Confederate States of America under Jefferson Davis
Confederate guns fire on Fort Sumter — the North now had a flag to rally round

config.why: The election had not started the war; it had removed the last reason for the South to stay — a president whose party existed to stop slavery's expansion would appoint the territories' officials, judges and postmasters.

activities.anchor: The South's task was easier in theory
activities.caption: file each fact — weight or hope?
activities.name: acwArithmeticBuckets

config.prompt: The arithmetic of 1861 — file each fact:

items.label: about 22 million people against 9 million, nearly 4 million of them enslaved and watched closely
the overwhelming majority of the country's firearms and cloth manufacture
over two-thirds of the railway mileage, and virtually the whole navy
survive long enough to be recognised — the easier-in-theory task
'King Cotton diplomacy' — Britain, the great textile power, intervening

config.why: The blockade strangled cotton exports and imports; Britain had a cotton surplus in 1861, developed Egypt and India as suppliers, and would not intervene for slavery after the Emancipation Proclamation.

activities.anchor: Turning weight into victory took time and blood
activities.caption: call the toll — the hinge of July 1863
activities.name: acwGettysburgEstimate

config.prompt: Gettysburg (1–3 July 1863), the costliest battle ever fought in the western hemisphere, cost roughly how many casualties?
config.why: About 51,000 — and July 1863 was the hinge: Gettysburg ended Lee's second invasion of the North, and Vicksburg's surrender on 4 July cut the Confederacy in half along the Mississippi.
config.context: The Emancipation Proclamation brought roughly 180,000 Black soldiers into Union blue — one tenth of the Union army by 1865.

activities.name: acwAmendmentsCloze

activities.anchor: For exam purposes the deepest debate is over
activities.caption: drag the divider — inevitable or blundered into?
activities.name: acwDebateCompare

config.prompt: Was 1861 unavoidable? Drag the divider between the two readings:

before.label: irrepressible conflict
before.text: 1861 as the unavoidable result of an irrepressible conflict over a labour system — slavery made the quarrel permanent.

after.label: politics failed
after.text: A broken party system, extremists on both wings, blunders like the Kansas-Nebraska Act — a solvable dispute ran out of road.

config.why: The evidence fits a middle reading: the specific deadlock of the 1850s — a South that would accept no limits and a North that would accept no expansion — made compromise impossible.
